subject: fix-read-only-hardening
body:
## Description

R2: Each mutating method of a read-only SQLite backend raises ReadOnlyStoreError.
R3: Reading through a read-only SQLite backend leaves the database file byte-identical.

Reviewer follow-up: a read-only read in a data directory that cannot create the WAL shared-memory file raises StoreError, not a raw sqlite3 error. A read-only read adds no file other than the `-wal` and `-shm` sidecars. Every backend mutator, including `delete_history_snapshot` and `import_op`, raises ReadOnlyStoreError.

## Approach

In `_connect_read_only`, run one probe query and convert `sqlite3.OperationalError` into `StoreError`. Add tests to `tests/canon/test_read_only_backend.py` first and record red. State the sidecar fact in the `open_backend` docstring.
title: Harden read-only reads

subject: read-only-backend
body:
## Description

R1: A read-only SQLite backend connection rejects a write statement.
R2: Each mutating method of a read-only SQLite backend raises ReadOnlyStoreError.
R3: Reading through a read-only SQLite backend leaves the database file byte-identical.
R4: A read-only SQLite backend on a missing database raises StoreNotInitializedError.
R5: A read-only SQLite backend returns the committed records while another connection holds a write transaction.

## Approach

Add `ReadOnlyStoreError(StoreError)` to `orchestra/canon/errors.py`. Add `read_only: bool = False` to `open_backend` and `SqliteBackend.__init__`. In read-only mode skip `_initialize_database` in `__init__`. In `_connect`, raise `StoreNotInitializedError` when the database file is missing, open `file:<db>?mode=ro` with `uri=True`, set `PRAGMA busy_timeout` and `PRAGMA query_only=ON`, and skip `mkdir`, `journal_mode` and `synchronous`. Guard `transaction`, `write_config`, `write_snapshot`, `init` and `backup` with a helper that raises `ReadOnlyStoreError`. Keep the edits to `sqlite_backend.py` narrow. Write tests in `tests/canon/test_read_only_backend.py` against temporary stores first and record red before the implementation.
title: Read-only SQLite backend

subject: read-only-project
body:
## Description

R6: open_store(directory, read_only=True) returns a Project with read_only True.
R7: Each write method of a read-only Project raises ReadOnlyStoreError.
R8: A read-only Project returns the same read results as a normal Project.
R9: open_store(directory, read_only=True) on a store with no database file raises StoreNotInitializedError.

## Approach

Add `read_only: bool = False` to the `Project` dataclass and to `open_store`. Thread it through `_open_bound`, `_open` and `_has_config`; in read-only mode `_has_config` and the global-binding config load read metadata through `MetadataFiles` so no backend constructor touches the database. `_open` raises `StoreNotInitializedError` in read-only mode when the backend reports no database file. Route every `open_backend(self.store_path)` call in `Project` through one helper that passes `read_only`. Raise `ReadOnlyStoreError` at the top of `create`, `update`, `supersede`, `correct`, `apply` and `apply_at_snapshot`. Write tests in `tests/canon/test_read_only_open.py` first, including the cross-process test `test_r10_read_only_project_reads_during_concurrent_write` for the verification task, and record red before the implementation.
title: Read-only Project open

subject: verify-read-only-open
body:
## Description

Prove the phase exit criteria hold together. R10 is the integration check through `open_store`. R11 is the full canon tree. R12 is the static gates.

R10: A read-only Project opened through open_store returns the committed records while a separate process writes through a normal Project.
R11: The existing tests in tests/canon pass.
R12: Static analysis (type check, lint, format) passes on the change.

## Approach

Run the three acceptance commands in the phase worktree. Do not edit the tree.
title: Verify read-only open

subject: verify-read-only-open-static
verify_command: uv run basedpyright && uvx ruff@0.13.1 check . && uvx ruff@0.13.1 format --check .
